Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second chapter to unfold! The umpires are on their way to take their respective positions, followed by the players of Pakistan. Quinton de Kock will be opening with Lhuan-dre Pretorius for the Proteas. Shaheen Afridi will start with the new ball. Away we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The stage is now set for the second half of the match. With 269 runs on the board, Pakistan have a challenging total to defend, and the focus now shifts to their bowling attack. South Africa's batters will look to build on the momentum created by their bowlers and successfully chase the target. The match hangs in the balance so far. Will the Proteas' batting unit overcome the total, or will Pakistan's bowlers rise to the occasion and secure a victory? We shall find out soon. Chase is coming up shortly...

A late, aggressive assault by Mohammad Nawaz and Faheem Ashraf provided the much-needed impetus in the death overs, allowing Pakistan to reach a par total of 269 runs. Nawaz scored 59 runs, and Wasim helped the team with a couple of boundaries in the death overs. South Africa's bowlers executed their plan well, maintaining tight control throughout the innings. The standout performer was pacer Nandre Burger, who tore through the lineup to finish with an excellent four-wicket haul. Corbin Bosch and Nqabayomzi Peter also contributed effectively, chipping in with important wickets.

Pakistan ended up with 269 on the board! Their batting lineup struggled early on, losing key wickets quickly. However, Saim Ayub showed great composure and, along with Salman Agha, built a crucial 92-run partnership for the fourth wicket, stabilizing the innings. Ayub anchored the middle overs, reaching a well-made half-century before falling for 53 in the 25th over. Agha then carried on, playing a slower, yet important, knock of 69 runs before his departure in the 41st over, which set the stage for the final push.

PITCH REPORT - Rameez Raja is pitchside with his insights. He says that the track seems to be better than the last game, with a nice covering of grass, which will certainly offer some good bounce to the pacers. Although it's still abrasive and has a few cracks, the conditions do appear to favor batting, so he reckons that Pakistan's decision to bat first is the right call.

Matthew Breetzke, skipper of South Africa, says that they would have batted first, judging the pitch, the ball will come nicely to the willow, but now they will have to shift their plan to restrict them to a decent total and then chase it down. Continues that the crowd is electrifying like their previous game. Ends up saying that they have two changes in the team as Nqabayomzi Peter and Nandre Burger come in for Lungi Ngidi and Lizaad Williams.

Skipper of Pakistan, Shaheen Afridi, says that they will be batting first as the pitch looks quite similar to the previous one. Continues that there's slightly more grass, which they reckon will help the ball come onto the bat nicely. Adds that they have made two changes, with Abrar Ahmed and Hasan Nawaz giving way to Faheem Ashraf and Mohammad Wasim. Ends up saying that they have identified areas for improvement, but the boys played well in the last game, which ultimately led to the victory.

South Africa, despite the loss, showed glimpses of strong intent but couldn’t close out the chase. Matthew Breetzke looked lively at the upper middle order, and the bowling attack had moments of sting, but they lacked that last push in the second inning. Today, they’ll look forward to build partnerships early with their openers, Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Quinton de Kock. Both batters provided hefty knocks and would like to replicate in this match as well. Their bowling order unit did a decent job as well, but skipper, Matthew Breetzke and company will need to have a plan to deal with the middle order of their opposition. Will Pakistan bag another win to seize the glory? Or will the Proteas make a comeback? Let's find out together. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

Pakistan carried momentum into this series after a hard-earned win in the opener, chasing down 264 with eight wickets down in 49.4 overs. Salman Agha played a key knock of 62 and Mohammad Rizwan chipped in with 55 as their batting found form under pressure. Their bowling held firm in the first inning. Pakistan will aim to maintain that composure and consolidate early to put South Africa on the back foot.

Welcome to a pivotal moment in the three-match ODI series as South Africa square off against Pakistan for the second ODI at Iqbal Stadium, Faisalabad. With Pakistan already grabbing the first game, South Africa will be out to level the series, and Pakistan will look to extend their advantage on home soil.
... MATCHDAY ...

International cricket returned to Faisalabad after 17 long years, and Pakistan marked the occasion with a win to go 1-0 up in the three-game series. It was also Shaheen Afridi’s first game as the full-time ODI captain. Pakistan will look to seal the series with another win in the 2nd ODI at the Iqbal Stadium. South Africa had their moments but were edged out by the hosts and will now aim to take the series to a decider. The Proteas began well with the bat before losing momentum in the middle overs, leaving a few runs out there. That proved costly as Pakistan, though it got a bit too close for comfort, managed the highest successful run chase in ODIs in Faisalabad. Despite the defeat, there were positives for the second-string Proteas side. None bigger than Quinton de Kock’s 63, his first notable score since returning to international cricket. Lhuan-dre Pretorius impressed with a fifty on his ODI debut. With Dewald Brevis sidelined by a shoulder muscle strain, the visitors will depend on Tony de Zorzi, Donovan Ferreira and captain Matthew Breetzke to step up. As he has done throughout the tour, Corbin Bosch made an impact with both bat and ball in the first game. The Proteas will rely on Lungi Ngidi and Lizaad Williams with the new ball, but with conditions expected to assist spinners, George Linde and Bjorn Fortuin will have to carry much of the load. From Pakistan’s perspective, they too, like South Africa, had a wobble after a promising start, but Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Agha held firm to take the chase forward. However, neither could take the side past the finish line, and if they find themselves in a similar position in the second ODI, they will want to see it through this time. The same applies to Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub, who got starts but failed to convert. It has been a tale of inconsistency for Babar Azam across formats, and that one big score is still missing. As one of Pakistan’s better players of spin, he will have an important role to play if conditions are dry and assist the spinners. Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah could not make early inroads with the new ball in the series opener, something they will want to correct. Abrar Ahmed made good use of favourable conditions, while Ayub continues to make an impact with the ball, even if he has not had much success with the bat lately. Despite missing several key players, the Proteas demonstrated that they are capable of challenging this strong Pakistan side in their den. Can Pakistan close out the series, or will South Africa bounce back to take it to a decider? We shall find out.
